subject: Orchid AI - Concurrency acceptance + probe credentials and windows
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@orchid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 17:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: performance targets + next steps for customer-led run

Hey Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned for the customer-led load rehearsal: 

Goals / SLOs (what Orchid asked us to validate)
- 95th percentile end-to-end generation latency <= 150 ms (inference-only target; include tokenization overhead where applicable)
- Sustained throughput target: ~1,200 requests/sec for non-streaming endpoints (burstable to 1,800 for short windows)
- Streaming concurrency: 200 simultaneous streaming sessions (chunked SSE or WebSocket token streaming)
- Error budget: <0.5% 5xx across the window

Run details we need from you
1) Preferred test window(s) (time zone please)
2) Test account / API key for the probe (we will treat keys as ephemeral)
3) Traffic origin IP ranges (or attach an allowlist file) so we can add temporary firewall rules
4) Whether you’ll provide k6 or Locust scripts; if not, we can run the supplied traffic matrix from your sample payloads
5) Any non-standard streaming behavior (large initial system messages, long-lived connections, or chunk sizes)

Suggested Redwood prep (what we’ll do)
- Reserve a dedicated pool for the window and pre-warm KV cache with representative prefixes
- Run a 30-minute smoke run 45 minutes before the official start to validate auth/allowlist
- Monitor 95th/99th latencies, tail memory, and token churn in real time; we’ll provide a short post-run dashboard

Can you confirm the window you prefer and attach the allowlist + the script you plan to run? If you want, drop the k6/locust file into the Drive link I shared and I’ll pull it ahead of time.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0126

From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@orchid.ai>

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance targets + next steps for customer-led run

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the following from Orchid's side: 

1) Test window: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 09:00–12:00 PST (we can shift to 13:00–16:00 if that works better for your ops)
2) Test account: orchid-ci@orchid.ai (we’ll create a time-limited API key and share it below)
3) IP ranges: attached (orchid_allowlist.txt) — tests will originate from our cloud provider (AWS us-west-2) and our on-prem agents (two /27 ranges listed)
4) Scripts: we have a k6 V1 script that mirrors our production traffic pattern; attaching orchid-k6-v1.js. If you prefer Locust, we can convert but k6 is the canonical one for this run.
5) Streaming: we use chunked SSE for token streaming. Typical session length is 45–120s; average token emission rate ~70 tokens/sec, peaks 200 tokens/sec for bursts.

API key (ephemeral): API key: ORCH-TST-XXXX (valid 2026-12-02 08:00–16:00 PST)

We’ll also plan a 30-minute dry run at 08:15 PST to validate allowlisting and auth. I’ve uploaded the two files to the shared Drive and attached locally as well.

Thanks — Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Soto <alex.soto@orchid.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance targets + next steps for customer-led run

Looping in some infra prep notes from my side — a few asks so we don’t hit last-minute blockers: 

- Please confirm exact origin CIDRs from the attached allowlist (Alex, the file lists two /27s and AWS us-west-2 public IP pools — we need the explicit ranges to pre-populate the firewall).
- Ports/protocols: we’ll need outbound access to 443 (HTTPS) and for streaming we’ll terminate SSE over TLS on the same port; no extra ports expected.
- TLS / ALPN: confirm you support standard TLS1.2+ with SNI (we already support it)
- Payloads: can you share typical request/response size (median and 95th) so we can size network egress and tokenizers? If you can paste a representative JSON request and the typical streaming behavior (e.g., initial large system prompt + steady tokens), that helps.
- Pre-population: we’ll pre-warm the model’s KV cache with the 10 most common prefixes you’ll test; supply a small prefix list if you have it.

Operational plan I’ll execute:
- Lock a dedicated pool with the "q8_0" quant profile for the window.
- Provision observability (per-route traces + token-level breakdowns) and add a 15s TTL on cache checks for the dry run.
- Add a 08:15 dry run + 08:30 smoke test before the official start; we’ll stop traffic automatically if error rate > 1% during the first 15 minutes.

If everything above looks good I’ll ask our network team to add the allowlist entries tomorrow morning and push a runbook to the shared Drive.

—Ben
